title: Movable obstruction interfering with stance but out of bounds
question: Jezz’s ball is in bounds, but a movable obstruction that is out of bounds interferes with his stance. He removes the movable obstruction. What is the ruling?
explanation: Under Rule 15.2a, a player may remove a movable obstruction anywhere on or off the course without penalty.

juniorVersion.title: Moving Something in the Way Even If It's Out of Bounds
juniorVersion.question: Jezz's ball is on the golf course, but something he can move, like a can, is just outside the course and gets in the way of where he stands. Jezz moves it out of the way. What happens now?

choices.text: Jezz gets one extra shot as a penalty.
Jezz does not get any penalty.

juniorVersion.explanation: You can move things like cans or bottles out of your way, even if they are off the course. You don't get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Something on or near the golf course like a can or bottle, that you can pick up and move.
A place outside the golf course where you are not supposed to play.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Let children practise spotting things they can and cannot move, like twigs or bins, and teach why out of bounds things can be moved, too.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they can't move things that are out of bounds, even if those things are in their way.
Children may worry about getting a penalty for moving things that are off the course.
